args.title: checkout-api health check failures after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks immediately after the latest deploy of v2.3.1 to production. At detection, all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) were on v2.3.1 and the service was unhealthy with an error rate of ~18%.

Action taken: Rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release previously healthy in production. The first rollback attempt partially failed (halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving a mixed-version fleet: us-east on v2.3.0, us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1). A retry completed the rollout to all three regions.

Current state: v2.3.0 is live in all production regions, service is healthy, error rate down to ~0.2%. No change-manager approval was required because v2.3.0 had previously been healthy in production.

Follow-up: Root cause of the v2.3.1 regression is not yet known; the version remains suspect and should not be re-deployed until investigated. Also worth reviewing why the rollback orchestrator errored mid-rollout, since that left the fleet in a mixed state temporarily.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
Task complete. The incident did go through despite the timeout — INC-0001 exists and is open, so I did not retry and risk a duplicate page.

**Summary:**

1. **Diagnosed:** checkout-api was on v2.3.1 in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), unhealthy with an ~18% error rate. Release history showed v2.3.0 as the most recent release that had been healthy in production (v2.3.1-rc in the list is a staging release and also unhealthy, so it was not a candidate).

2. **Rolled back to v2.3.0.** The first attempt errored partway with "Rollback halted after us-east: orchestrator error," leaving a mixed fleet — us-east on v2.3.0, us-west and eu-west still on the failing v2.3.1. I verified the partial state, then retried; the second attempt rolled out cleanly to all three regions. No change-manager approval was needed since v2.3.0 had previously been healthy in production.

3. **Verified:** service is healthy, v2.3.0 in all regions, error rate down from ~18% to ~0.2%.

4. **Opened SEV2 incident INC-0001** describing the symptoms, the rollback (including the partial failure and retry), the current healthy state, and two follow-ups: v2.3.1's root cause is unknown and it should not be re-deployed until investigated, and the rollback orchestrator's mid-rollout error is worth reviewing since it briefly left production in a mixed-version state.

One note: the incident-create call returned a 30s timeout but the incident was in fact recorded — I verified via `list_incidents` rather than retrying, which is why I used an idempotency key and checked before acting.
